memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses placed the gold altar in the tent of meeting in front of the curtain and burned fragrant incense on it, as the Lord commanded him. Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle." - Exod 40:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The incense altar stood immediately in front of the curtain — closer to God's presence than anything except the ark itself. And the first thing Moses did after placing it was burn incense on it.

Scripture tells us plainly what this represents. In Revelation, golden bowls of incense are the prayers of God's people (Rev 5:8), and incense is offered with the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar before the throne (Rev 8:3-4).

So the position of that altar is a statement. Prayer brings us nearer to God than almost anything else we do.

Think about what that means for your praying. The rushed prayers on the way to work. The wordless ones when you have nothing left. The ones repeated for years with no visible answer. Heaven describes them as fragrance rising.

Notice this altar was not for sacrifice. Nothing died here. Blood was dealt with outside at the bronze altar; here there was only fragrance. Because the sacrifice was made, the prayer could rise.

That is our position exactly. We pray with confidence not because our words are eloquent but because Christ's blood has already opened the way (Heb 10:19-22).

Your prayers reach further than you feel.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe your ordinary prayers actually reach God?
2. What prayer have you given up on that you should take up again?
3. Would prayer be described as central or occasional in your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my prayers rise before You as fragrance. Draw me closer through them. Amen.
